answer: Tide-Station Pulse Grove: each identity posts a $40 buoy-registration bond and is bound to one of NOAA's ~200 live tide stations. Every epoch it must quote that station's water level within 2 cm, pulled inside a 10-minute window. The verifier re-pulls the same station from NOAA's public feed and rejects any mismatch, so a copied reading fails at once. With only ~200 stations in the ocean, a farm runs out of distinct gauges long before it scales, and a wrong quote forfeits the bond. Honest agents pay one bond and read one gauge; the tide keeps its own pulse, and no photocopy of it passes.
